lessons.title: Hypoglycemia: Brain Fuel Emergency
lessons.summary: glucose is a fast reversible cause of altered mental status, seizure and focal neurologic mimic.

sections.title: 1) Symptoms
paragraphs: Adrenergic symptoms include sweating, tremor and palpitations; neuroglycopenia causes confusion, behavior change, seizure, coma or focal deficits. Beta-blockers may blunt warning symptoms.

sections.title: 2) Confirm and treat
paragraphs: Check point-of-care glucose early in altered patients. If low with symptoms, treat promptly with oral carbohydrate when safe or IV/IO glucose/glucagon according to protocol.

sections.title: 3) Find the cause
paragraphs: Insulin/sulfonylurea, missed meals, renal/liver failure, sepsis, alcohol and adrenal disease are common contexts.

sections.title: 4) Rebound risk
paragraphs: Long-acting insulin/sulfonylurea or systemic illness can cause recurrence; a normal glucose after treatment does not always make discharge safe.

lessons.title: DKA & HHS: Fluids, Potassium, Insulin and Cerebral Risk
lessons.summary: hyperglycemic crisis is a fluid/electrolyte/acid-base emergency—not just a high glucose number.

sections.title: 1) DKA physiology
paragraphs: Insulin deficiency + counter-regulatory hormones → lipolysis/ketones → metabolic acidosis, osmotic diuresis and dehydration. Total-body potassium is depleted despite normal/high serum K.

sections.title: 2) HHS
paragraphs: Usually profound hyperglycemia/hyperosmolality and dehydration with less ketosis; neurologic dysfunction may be prominent.

sections.title: 3) Treatment sequence concept
paragraphs: Volume resuscitation, potassium-aware insulin therapy and treatment of precipitating cause. Starting insulin without understanding potassium can be dangerous.

sections.title: 4) Prehospital priorities
paragraphs: ABC, ECG, glucose, perfusion, mental status, cautious protocol-based fluids and rapid transport. Avoid empiric insulin outside authorized protocol.

lessons.title: Adrenal Crisis: Refractory Shock, Hyponatremia & Hypoglycemia
lessons.summary: consider adrenal crisis in unexplained shock—especially known adrenal disease/steroid dependence.

sections.title: 1) Why shock occurs
paragraphs: Cortisol deficiency impairs vascular responsiveness and glucose homeostasis; mineralocorticoid deficiency can cause sodium loss, volume depletion and hyperkalemia in primary adrenal failure.

sections.title: 2) Clues
paragraphs: Hypotension/shock, weakness, abdominal symptoms, vomiting, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia and hyperkalemia; history of adrenal insufficiency or chronic steroid withdrawal is high yield.

sections.title: 3) Treatment concept
paragraphs: Rapid isotonic fluid, glucose if needed and stress-dose corticosteroid are central once suspected; exact regimen follows protocol.

sections.title: 4) Trigger
paragraphs: Infection, surgery, trauma, vomiting or missed steroids can precipitate crisis.

lessons.title: Thyroid Storm & Myxedema Coma
lessons.summary: opposite endocrine extremes can both produce cardiovascular and neurologic collapse.

sections.title: 1) Thyroid storm
paragraphs: Severe thyrotoxicosis with hyperthermia, tachyarrhythmia, heart failure, GI/hepatic dysfunction and delirium. Triggered by infection, surgery, stopping therapy and other stressors.

sections.title: 2) Myxedema coma
paragraphs: Severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, hyponatremia and altered consciousness.

sections.title: 3) EMS focus
paragraphs: Support airway/ventilation, temperature, glucose, rhythm and perfusion; avoid overly aggressive active warming in severe hypothyroid shock; definitive endocrine therapy is hospital-based.
